item.text: I'll start by reading the task input and understanding the OpenSpec detect workflow.

I can't complete this — the environment's filesystem sandbox is failing before any command or file operation runs, so I have no way to read `/task-input/task.md`, inspect the repo, or write artifacts.

Evidence (all attempts fail identically, regardless of `cmd`, `workdir`, shell, or login mode):

- `exec_command` with even `pwd` / `true` →
  `bwrap: Can't mkdir /workspace/.codex: Read-only file system`
- `view_image` on `/task-input/task.md` → same bwrap helper error
- `apply_patch` adding a probe file → `Failed to write file /workspace/sandbox_probe.txt`

Diagnosis: the fs sandbox helper (bwrap) cannot create its `/workspace/.codex` directory because `/workspace` is mounted read-only inside the sandbox namespace, so every read, write, and exec is blocked. This is a mount/permission configuration problem in the task environment, not something I can work around: approval policy is `never` and I was instructed not to pass `sandbox_permissions`, so escalation isn't available either.

State of the workspace: unchanged. No files were created or modified (the probe write failed), no tests were run, and no planning artifacts were written, since writes are impossible in this state.

To unblock, the environment needs `/workspace` (or at least the method planning mount) writable inside the sandbox — e.g. fix the read-only bind of `/workspace` or pre-create `/workspace/.codex` as a writable mountpoint. Once file access works, I'll read `/task-input/task.md`, identify repository-relative candidate test paths with their symbols and reasons, and write exactly one `detection-draft.json` (only a `candidates` array, each entry with `path`, `symbols`, `reason`) plus the other method planning artifacts into that same mounted planning directory.
